beats.text: Denisovans, an extinct human species, roamed Siberia from 200,000 to 32,000 years ago.
beats.say: Denisovans, an extinct human species, roamed Siberia from 200,000 to 32,000 years ago.

beats.text: Found in Siberia's Denisova Cave, their DNA reveals dark skin and a distinct build.

beats.text: Denisova Cave, in south-central Siberia, yielded the first Denisovan remains.

beats.text: Other Denisovans were found in caves in China and Laos, expanding their known range.

beats.text: No formal species name has been established, but they are closely related to Neanderthals.

beats.text: Facts: The first Denisovan remains were found in Siberia's Denisova Cave, and DNA evidence suggests they had dark skin and a distinct build. They interbred with modern humans, with high levels of Denisovan DNA in Melanesians. The Harbin cranium, identified as Denisovan in 2025, confirms their presence in China.

facts.claim: The first Denisovan remains were found in Siberia's Denisova Cave.
facts.quote: The first Denisovans discovered were known from few physical remains.

facts.claim: Denisovans interbred with modern humans, with high levels of Denisovan DNA in Melanesians.
facts.quote: Denisovans interbred with modern humans, with a high percentage (roughly 5%) of Denisovan DNA occurring in Melanesians, Aboriginal Australians, and Filipino Negritos.

facts.claim: The Harbin cranium, identified as Denisovan in 2025, confirms their presence in China.
facts.quote: Fu et al. (2025) also retrieved 95 endogenous proteins from the same specimen, and suggested that H. longi can be confidently assigned to a Denisovan population.
